summary: Reading JClaw's harness history rather than its harness, three defect classes recur, each closed only after it shipped: (1) an instruction file drifts away from the code it describes — 0dfcd451 corrected SIX contradicted claims in AGENTS.md at once, found by review, with the drift having propagated into build.gradle.kts and the pre-push comments; (2) a detector is written in a dialect its engine does not speak, so it reports CLEAN forever — f588bc44, where `git grep -nE` silently treats \b \d \s as literals and the credential battery measured 0 of 9 planted secrets against -P's 9 of 9; (3) a gate-guard that matches raw substrings of a config file passes when the line it guards is commented out or moved — 88b142ee. All three are false-PASS classes, which is the only kind that costs nothing to ignore and everything to have. MEASURED ON OUR SIDE: class (2) reproduces on this machine (`git grep -E '\d'` matched `abcd`, `git grep -P '\d'` matched `abc 123`) but we use `git grep -E` nowhere, so it is a hazard with no live site; class (3) DOES have a live site — tests/chaosGate.test.ts:73 reads the runner's plant count with an unanchored regex that a comment satisfies; class (1) has a live, dated, 9-day-old instance (see study-agent-instructions.json).

candidates.pattern: Instruction-file rot is a recurring defect with a measurable cost, not a tidiness issue
candidates.failurePrevented: Rules that every agent reads quietly stop being true; the drift then propagates into code comments and build scripts, so three places agree on something false.
candidates.jclawEvidence: Commit 0dfcd451 2026-09-06 `docs(agents): correct six claims the epic review found the code contradicts (JCLAW-1148)`, body: `Nullness: ... The text said the opposite, and the build-script and pre-push comments repeated it.` · `Frozen stores: with allowStoreUpdate pinned off, a fixed site fails the build until its store line is deleted; the text said the store prunes itself.` DIFFSTAT CORRECTED: `git show --numstat 0dfcd451` gives AGENTS.md +59/-37 across 3 files changed, 65 insertions, 43 deletions. An earlier draft of this file wrote '+96/-43', which glued two denominators together — 96 is AGENTS.md's TOTAL changed lines (59+37) and 43 is the repo-wide deletion count.
candidates.builtAndExercised: Closed by REVIEW, not by a gate — there is no test in JClaw that checks AGENTS.md against the code. The stamp at AGENTS.md:6 did not prevent it; the six false claims lived inside the stamped block.
candidates.ourEvidence: See study-agent-instructions.json / agent-instructions-1: CLAUDE.md:67 has named a deleted file since 995bb52 (2026-09-08).
candidates.proposal: Merged into agent-instructions-1 — this candidate is the evidence that the class recurs, not a second gate.
candidates.why: It converts agent-instructions-1 from 'we found one' into 'this class recurs in a repo that reviews harder than we do' — which is the difference between a tidy-up and a gate.

candidates.pattern: A detector must be shown capable of matching before a zero from it is reported
candidates.failurePrevented: A scan written in a regex dialect its engine does not implement matches nothing, and the resulting CLEAN is believed precisely because it looks like health.
candidates.jclawEvidence: Commit f588bc44 2026-08-15 `fix(secret-scan): the documented invocation could not match anything`: `On macOS git (Apple Git 2.50.1) the ERE engine silently ignores \b, \d and \s — no error, no warning, just zero matches. Fifteen of the sixteen CRITICAL patterns are \b-anchored ... The lone exception was the PEM pattern ... which is exactly why the failure looked like a clean repo rather than a broken tool.` Measured in the body: `-E detected 0 of 9 / -P detected 9 of 9`. The durable fix is the control, .claude/commands/secret-scan.md:40 `**Prove the harness before trusting a zero.** ... A pass that has not been shown capable of matching is not evidence of absence`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: Yes — the control is a mandatory documented step whose result the report template must state, added in the same commit as the fix. Honest limit: it is enforced by instruction, not by a test.
candidates.ourEvidence: The dialect hazard REPRODUCES: in a throwaway repo holding `abcd` and `abc 123`, `git grep -nE '\d'` returned `f.txt:1:abcd` (literal d) while `git grep -nP '\d'` returned `f.txt:2:abc 123`. NUANCE: this is git's own ERE, not the platform grep's — `/usr/bin/grep -E` here does honour the escapes, so the trap does not generalise to our `grep -E` gates. THE 'NO LIVE SITE' SEARCH WAS UNDER-SPECIFIED, and an adversarial lens caught it with this cluster's own defect: `grep -rn 'git grep -E'` misses the spelling `git grep -n -E`, which occurs at docs/research/runs/wf_99c74d25-624-LEDGER.md:445. A probe whose pattern cannot match the real spelling reports a clean zero — the exact failure this candidate is about, committed inside its own evidence. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES the re-run: that single hit is an archived transcript line inside a document, and its pattern uses only `\.` and `\(`, escaped literals ERE handles correctly. Still no live hazard site. The control DISCIPLINE we mostly have: tests/claimcheck.test.ts:334-335 floors the corpus at >1600 cites / >350 values; tests/chaosGate.test.ts:73 reads the runner's own constant. One unguarded zero-reporter remains — .githooks/pre-commit:40 (agent-instructions-4).
candidates.proposal: None beyond agent-instructions-4. Record the `git grep -E` hazard as a pitfall line rather than a gate, since we have nothing to guard.
candidates.why: The discipline is already ours and already applied; the specific macOS trap has zero live sites here. Adopting the fix we do need (the `|| true`) and dropping the rest loudly is the honest split.

candidates.pattern: A gate that reads a config or source file by raw substring passes when the line it guards is commented out
candidates.failurePrevented: The guard on a guard reads its value out of a COMMENT, so the live value can be anything the comment is not. SEVERITY CORRECTED after an independent experiment: the consequence this test exists to prevent — a silently shrinking chaos gate — is independently pinned from the other side by tests/chaosGate.test.ts:66-68 `expect(ALL).toHaveLength(43)`, which counts plants by static import, and a literal drift (43→40) is caught loudly by the runner itself at scripts/gates/chaos.ts:165. The exploitable window is therefore NARROW: the live line must become a form the regex cannot parse (a computed or env-driven expression) AND a stale literal comment must sit above it — which is also the only shape that makes chaos.ts:165 vacuous.
candidates.jclawEvidence: Commit 88b142ee 2026-09-06 `test(gates): close the silent switch-offs the conformance tests could not see`: `Both gate conformance tests matched raw substrings of build.gradle.kts, so enabled.set(false), disable("NullAway"), an excludedPaths option, or a required line moved into a comment all passed. They now strip comments first, assert the ERROR line inside the compileJava block rather than anywhere in the file, and fail on each of the known switch-offs.` Same commit: `The Lucene scan accepted a release anywhere in the file, including at the end of a test body where a failing assertion skips it`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: Yes — the fix ships the negative cases as assertions ('fail on each of the known switch-offs'), i.e. the gate's own false-pass modes became tests.
candidates.ourEvidence: LIVE SITE verified byte-for-byte: tests/chaosGate.test.ts:73 is `    const found = /const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);/.exec(src)?.[1];` — no `^`, no `m` flag, `.exec` takes the first match. scripts/gates/chaos.ts:81 is `const EXPECTED_TOTAL = 43;`. THE FALSE PASS IS MEASURED, twice independently: with `// const EXPECTED_TOTAL = 43;` above a live `const EXPECTED_TOTAL = Number(process.env.CHAOS_TOTAL ?? 43);`, the regex reads 43 out of the comment and `expect(found).toBe('43')` PASSES. Remove the comment and it returns undefined and fails closed, so the fail-closed direction is confirmed by execution rather than reasoned.
candidates.proposal: STRIP COMMENTS FIRST, then match — and reuse what exists rather than writing a second stripper: `splitLines` in scripts/gates/claimcheckLib.ts already separates code from comments (a hand-rolled scanner that knows `//`, `/* */` and string literals) and is already pinned by claimcheck's own tests. `const code = splitLines(src).map((l) => l.code).join('\n')`, then `[...code.matchAll(/^const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);$/gm)]` asserted to have exactly ONE match. CORRECTION: an earlier draft proposed the anchored regex ALONE. That is insufficient and it was measured — `^` anchors to a LINE start, and a line inside a `/* ... */` block also starts at column 0, so the anchored regex still reads 43 out of a block comment. Stripping is the fix JClaw itself shipped (88b142ee: 'They now strip comments first').
candidates.doneCriterion: Five cases, all measured with splitLines: clean → 1 match '43' GREEN · line-comment above a computed live value → 0 matches RED · block-comment above a computed live value → 0 matches RED · stale '43' comment above a live 40 → 1 match '40' RED · constant renamed → 0 matches RED.
candidates.cost: ~3 lines in one existing test; 0 runtime cost.
candidates.why: The one candidate in this unit with a live false-pass site in our own gate-guard, and the fix is three lines in a test that already exists.

candidates.pattern: A hook that names a cause must classify the failure first
candidates.failurePrevented: A release chases a fix that could not have worked, because the hook reported the failure it expected instead of the one that happened.
candidates.jclawEvidence: Commit 4a9208e3 2026-07-27 `fix(hooks): stop pre-push blaming import order for every spotlessCheck failure`; the resulting comment at .githooks/pre-push:100-103 `This hook used to report every such exit as "Import order drift", which sent the v0.17.8 release chasing a spotlessApply that could not have fixed it.`
candidates.builtAndExercised: Yes, shipped in response to a real misdiagnosed release.
candidates.ourEvidence: See hooks-ci-sandbox-3: our run_step names only the failing STEP and then prints the tool's own last 20 lines, so it cannot assert a wrong cause.
candidates.why: Already the shape we have; nothing to build.

candidates.pattern: The bounded-scope habit: each harness fix ships with the measurement that proves it, in the commit body
candidates.failurePrevented: A fix is believed because it is plausible; six months later nobody can tell whether it was ever measured.
candidates.jclawEvidence: f588bc44 body: `Measured, not assumed. Nine synthetic provider credentials ... were planted in a scratch file outside the repo and both engines run over it: -E detected 0 of 9 / -P detected 9 of 9`. 88b142ee body: `Verified: NullnessGateConformanceTest, ResourceLeakGateConformanceTest, PropertyBasedTest, TaskScopeTest and EvalRunnerTest pass.` 0dfcd451 body: six numbered claim-by-claim corrections.
candidates.builtAndExercised: It is a convention visible across the sampled commits, not a mechanism.
candidates.ourEvidence: The per-turn ship-bar contract (rule 3, 'VERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED ... with the output PASTED') and the repo's own commit history enforce this already; .githooks/pre-commit:36-38 even records the one time a commit message asserted a test total the hook had not measured.
candidates.why: Identical to a standing rule we already run under; naming it again buys nothing.

antiPatterns.what: Reading the volume of JClaw's harness history as a target to match.
antiPatterns.evidence: `git log -- .githooks/` alone is 16 commits; the conformance/arch/store/commands surface is 35+ in three months, across eight gate-guard test classes.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: That cadence is affordable for a repo with CI, a team and a ticket system. Here every gate is paid for in per-commit seconds and in the attention of one developer. The transferable unit is the DEFECT CLASS, not the count of guards.

antiPatterns.what: Concluding from f588bc44 that we should audit every regex in the repo for dialect traps.
antiPatterns.evidence: `grep -rn 'git grep -E'` over our shell, TS, MJS and markdown → empty; and /usr/bin/grep -E '\d' behaves correctly on this machine (matched `abc 123`, not `abcd`) — only *git's own* ERE engine is the trap.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: The lesson is the control, not the audit. An audit with no live site is the 'interesting' that the kickoff says to rank below 'has already bitten us'.

integrity: VERIFIED BY COMMAND at /tmp/jclaw pinned 366459cd: `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short` over .githooks/ (16 commits) and over test/*Conformance*.java, test/ArchitectureTest.java, archunit_store/, .claude/commands/ (35 shown); full bodies read with `git show --format=%B --no-patch` for 0dfcd451, f588bc44 and 88b142ee, plus `git show f588bc44 -- .claude/commands/secret-scan.md` for the diff hunk; 4a9208e3 taken from its subject line and from the resulting comment at .githooks/pre-push:98-113, which was read in full. OURS: the `git grep -E` vs `-P` dialect test run in a throwaway repo at /tmp/gtest against a two-line fixture (result pasted in the ourEvidence field); `grep -rn 'git grep -E'` over our tree → empty; tests/chaosGate.test.ts:60-95 read; scripts/gates/chaos.ts greps for EXPECTED_TOTAL (:81 literal, :165-169 the runner's own drift check). NOTE: the chaosGate false-pass in harness-evolution-3 is reasoned from the source and NOT yet executed — it is stated as a proposal with a done-criterion, and P4 must watch it go red before it is believed. ADVERSARIALLY REFUTED 2026-09-17 (C3-lensA.json, C1-lensA.json, C2-lensA.json). The chaosGate false pass was reproduced independently by a lens on file COPIES; the diffstat, the severity and the insufficiency of the first proposed fix are its corrections, each re-executed by the parent loop before acceptance.
